title: Finding a work order by typing its status still works
refs: SV-9160 (INV-02; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s4 - status DROPPED at spec v12 - PO DECISION)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. The four seeded work orders S9160-17580, S9160-17581, S9160-17582 and S9160-17583 exist for customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling'.
2. Open one of them and write down the status shown on it (for example Estimate, In Progress, Approved or Quality Check).
3. Work Orders access: View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the status word exactly as it appears on the work order, for example: Estimate
3. Read the Work orders group.
4. Clear the input and repeat with a two-word status typed as one word, for example: qualitycheck
5. Read the Work orders group again.
custom_expected:
Work orders in that status are returned by both forms.
In V1 the status word was part of what a work order could be found by - the underscore was removed (so 'in_progress' matched 'inprogress') and 'quality_check' also matched 'qualitycheckqc'. A dispatcher typing 'Estimate' into search got the estimates back.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test Blocked with the exact query you typed and what came back, and flag it - a task ticket goes to the Product Owner to confirm whether the loss is acceptable. Do not raise it as a defect until the PO has ruled, and do not pass the test just because the V2 specification allows the new behaviour.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:113-116, which folds wo.status into the work order search text). Version 1.5 of the Global Search - Product Requirements specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 4 does NOT list status among the indexed Work Order fields - it was removed at specification version 12.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM, so this case asserts the V1 behaviour and tells you to record and flag rather than guess.

custom_preconds:

title: Every matching type still appears when a search matches many records
refs: SV-9160 (INV-14, INV-15; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s5.2 20-result cap - PO DECISION)
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header click the Search box (it is a BUTTON, data-test-id global_search_trigger, not a typeable field) or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Global search opens as a CENTRED MODAL over the page: a text input at the top, then a scope tab strip - All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices - each showing its own result count, then results grouped by type with a count beside each heading (e.g. "Work orders (4)"). Esc closes the modal. NOTE: group headings are SENTENCE case in the build ("Work orders", "Part sales"). If a group shows nothing, click that entity's scope tab to confirm it really is 0 rather than scrolling. Modal behaviour verified on the V2 QA branch sv9160 on 14 September 2026.
1. Records exist matching the word ZZAUTOTEST across SEVERAL types at once: the customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', the asset owned by it, the vendor 'ZZAUTOTEST Kestrel Parts Supply', the part 'ZZAUTOTEST Brake Chamber Kestrel' and the four work orders S9160-17580 to S9160-17583.
2. Access to all of those areas: Work Orders View, Customers View, Vendors View, Catalog & Inventory View.
custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type: ZZAUTOTEST
3. Stay on the All tab and write down every group heading you can see, and its count.
4. Click each scope tab in turn - Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors - and write down the count on each.
5. Compare: is there any type that has matches on its own tab but shows NO rows and NO group on the All tab?
custom_expected:
Every type that has a match is represented on the All tab. No matching type is missing from the All view.
In V1 each type was given its own slots (up to three) and there was no overall limit, so if six types matched, all six were shown. V2 caps the whole result list at 20, so a type with real matches can be squeezed out entirely by a type that matches more often - the user sees nothing for it and believes the record does not exist.
IF THIS FAILS: it is a real V1-to-V2 capability loss. Mark the test Blocked with the exact query you typed and what came back, and flag it - a task ticket goes to the Product Owner to confirm whether the loss is acceptable. Do not raise it as a defect until the PO has ruled, and do not pass the test just because the V2 specification allows the new behaviour.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the V1 behaviour recorded in the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (useGlobalSearch.ts:152 (MAX_PER_TYPE = 3, applied per type) with no overall cap anywhere in the filter). Version 1.5 of the specification (Confluence page 576978945) section 5.2 caps counts and the result list at 20 and section 2 rules out pagination; the specification is SILENT on whether a matching type may be shown zero rows because of that cap.
Standing Rule 96 makes a V1 capability the default expectation and Standing Rule 58 makes a code-versus-document conflict a PO DECISION ITEM, so this case asserts the V1 behaviour and tells you to record and flag rather than guess.
